key_insight: A feedforward neural network trained on the writhe density matrix can classify the first six prime two-component links with high accuracy, showing that topology can be learned from geometric features.
engineering_relevance: This offers a fast, data-driven alternative to exact topological computations for polymer, DNA, and protein systems where link classification can be a bottleneck.
method: Build a writhe density matrix from polymer/link configurations
Train a feedforward neural network on thermally equilibrated examples
Test robustness across temperature, component length, and added Gaussian noise
evidence_signal: The model achieved 97% accuracy on thermally equilibrated configurations and stayed accurate across temperatures and link lengths, but performance dropped sharply under topology-altering Gaussian noise.
watch_item: The approach is sensitive to noise that changes topology, so its reliability may depend on how well the input configurations preserve the true link structure.
paper_title: Writhe-Based Polymer Link Classification Using Machine Learning
